subject.title: feat(slack): allow configurable App Home views

question: Should Slack App Home customization become a permanent process-stable configuration contract, or should OpenClaw retain only the built-in view?
rationale: The choice determines new public config keys, account precedence, restart/reload semantics, filesystem lifecycle, and the supported operator contract; repository evidence cannot select that product boundary safely.

options.title: Process-stable customization
options.body: Keep the feature but load and validate inline or file-backed views at startup or an explicit owner reload boundary rather than on every Slack event.

options.title: Accept live file reload
options.body: Keep per-event `viewPath` reads and explicitly own the resulting filesystem latency and availability contract with focused operational proof.

options.title: Retain built-in view only
options.body: Decline the new configuration surface and continue publishing the existing safe App Home view.

recommendation.title: Process-stable customization
recommendation.body: Keep the feature but load and validate inline or file-backed views at startup or an explicit owner reload boundary rather than on every Slack event.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current App Home lifecycle and are the strongest history-backed candidate to confirm how customization should fit it.
